transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (CSM), Leeza Patel (Redwood SE), Alicia Rivera (Lyra Head of Security), Tom O'Neil (Infra Lead), Dr. Sunita Rao (Compliance), Ben Carter (DevOps), Maya Li (Legal)

Summary / Topics (auto-generated) - may be incomplete.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we really appreciate you carving out time. quick round-robin?
[00:08] Alicia: hi — Alicia Rivera, head of security at Lyra. i'll be leading the compliance side here.
[00:12] Tom: tom o'neil, infra lead, i'll be hands on for any VPC / network topics.
[00:16] Sunita: sunita, compliance — SOC 2 and iso questions primarily.
[00:21] Jordan: great. priya's going to walk through the trust center and control mapping, leeza will cover evidence handoff, and marcus will handle access.
[00:30] Priya: hey all, so quick caveat — i'll do a high level first then dive into the artifacts. redwood's trust center is our central portal for compliance artifacts: SOC reports, penetration test summaries, architecture diagrams, and our control mappings. you can request temporary viewer access for your auditors.
[00:52] Alicia: when you say 'control mapping' do you map to iso 27001 as well as SOC 2? we have to feed both into our compliance tracker.
[00:59] Priya: yes — we maintain a dual mapping. the CSV links control ids to evidence artifacts and we include crosswalks for iso annex a and SOC 2 common criteria. sometimes the names in our exporter get munged — like, the internal tag for session-logging might read as 'aud logging' in the raw export —sorry, transcription joke — but we can clean that per your tracker.
[01:20] Dr. Sunita: that's good. our external auditor asked for a matrix of evidence by control owner and retention period. can you produce that?
[01:29] Priya: absolutely — i'll generate a controls matrix that includes artifact link, retention, owner, and the last time evidence was validated. we'll mark items that are Redwood-managed versus customer-managed.
[01:41] Tom: network question — for private deployment we need VPC peering and explicit egress filtering. how do you handle logs? do you provide a push or do we pull?
[01:52] Leeza: for Dedicated and Private we offer multiple patterns: push to your SIEM via secure forwarder, or you can pull logs from our signed S3 export. for hosted we retain detailed audit logs in the trust center with downloadable zips. retention policy can be tuned by plan — default is 90 days for detailed request/response traces, and 12 months for admin events, but we can extend per contract.
[02:22] Ben: we need 7 years for certain pharma traces — is that possible?
[02:26] Marcus: long-retention add-on is available; it requires archived encryption keys and lifecycle rules. costs apply and we can scope that.
[02:35] Alicia: encryption — we need assurance around customer key control. can you integrate with our KMS or HSM?
[02:43] Priya: yes. for Private deployments we support BYOK via customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and HSM integrations for on-prem. for hosted we offer envelope encryption with optional customer-managed keys (you bring the key and we do envelope encrypt). note: multi-region failover will require key replication or separate key policies per region.
[03:08] Tom: so if we pin data to eu-west-1, will key material stay in the EEA?
[03:12] Priya: yes — region pinning + customer-managed key in that region keeps key material in-region. there are some edge cases with cross-region backups — we can document them.
[03:22] Sunita: audit logs — what granularity do you keep? we need to show who accessed which artifact and when, ideally with IP and session id.
[03:31] Leeza: logs include username, role, action, timestamp, source IP, and request id for artifact access. for Trust Center downloads we store the audit trail with signed tokens. we can produce certified exports for auditors.
[03:45] Ben: and are those logs tamper-evident?
[03:48] Marcus: yes, we support append-only log buckets with object-versioning and MFA delete options; also we can ship periodic signed manifests to your SIEM so you have an independent record.
[04:02] Alicia: data residency — we will likely keep PHI in EEA only. does Redwood enforce region isolation for hosted?
[04:12] Priya: you can pin models and storage to specific regions in our platform. for workloads requiring strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated with region-constrained pools. hosted can be limited to region but customers should request the residency SLA in the contract.
[04:30] Tom: from a network perspective, we also need SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning. what's your recommended flow?
[04:38] Jordan: we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. most enterprise customers implement SCIM so groups and roles map automatically. we have templates for Okta, Azure AD, and JumpCloud.
[04:51] Maya: on legal — if auditors need raw transcripts or content, what's Redwood's stance on data sharing? we need contractual language.
[04:59] Jordan: we do not disclose customer content unless compelled by law. access for auditors typically follows two approaches: 1) you pull/download from your Trust Center evidence exports, or 2) we provide redacted extracts under an NDA and governed process. we'll loop in legal to create appropriate language.
[05:18] Sunita: do you have a SOC 2 Type II report available now?
[05:22] Jordan: yes, we do. i'll share the secure link to the report and the certificate. note: the Type II covers period through 2026-06-30.
[05:30] Alicia: excellent. can you also mark which controls are relevant for processing PHI?
[05:35] Priya: we'll flag PHI-relevant controls in the mapping CSV. also we'll annotate operational controls that require Lyra action, like client-side encryption or masking.
[05:46] Ben: curious about model cache and kv cache — does that persist across requests and is it considered stored data?
[05:54] Priya: default KV cache for generation is ephemeral to the session and not written to durable blob store unless you explicitly enable caching. we treat any durable caches as customer-managed for private deployments. for hosted we have configurable TTLs and an opt-in persistent cache that you can choose to encrypt with customer keys.
[06:18] Tom: what's the fastest way to get auditor access to artifacts?
[06:22] Marcus: we can grant temporary Trust Center viewer roles scoped to specific artifacts and set expirations. auditors can create a read-only account that logs their activity. alternatively, we can produce a signed artifact bundle and deliver via secure link.
[06:36] Alicia: how often do you refresh evidence? like pen tests and infra diagrams?
[06:40] Priya: pen tests are annual, infra diagrams are maintained with each major infra change and we have a six-month review cadence for architecture docs. we also publish a changelog in the trust center for artifacts.
[06:54] Sunita: for ISO 27001, do you have an ISMS policy package we can reference?
[06:59] Leeza: we provide the ISMS high-level policy suite in the Trust Center — it includes our scope statement, risk assessment summary, and statement of applicability. detailed internal risk registers are redacted, but we give the artifacts auditors typically need.
[07:14] Maya: legal question: if we get temporary access for auditors, can we limit export capability?
[07:19] Marcus: yes, we can disable downloads while keeping a view-only mode, and capture screenshots are outside our control but we log any viewing. we can also require export approvals for specific artifacts.
[07:33] Tom: SLA / incident response — if there's an incident, do you provide incident timelines and root cause?
[07:38] Jordan: incident response is part of our contract — we provide timeline summaries, RCA, and mitigation steps. severity-based SLA applies. for Dedicated/Private we can include a longer retention of incident artifacts.
[07:52] Alicia: valuation / assurance — do you have encryption at rest by default and key rotation?
[07:58] Priya: yes encryption at rest is default; rotating KEKs yearly is our standard. with customer-managed keys you control rotation cadence.
[08:06] Ben: small thing — for compliance we need proof that logs are immutable. what's the format for your signed manifests?
[08:13] Leeza: manifests are JSON lines with file checksums and a signed envelope. we can also provide PGP-signed manifests if your auditors prefer GPG chains.
[08:25] Sunita: do you support artifact-level retention rules so we can keep some advisory docs longer?
[08:29] Priya: yes, retention rules are per-artifact-type and can be customized per contract. by default admin-events 12 months, request traces 90 days, but we can archive longer.
[08:40] Alicia: one more — can we get an operations contact for the evidence handoff?
[08:44] Marcus: yeah that's leeza and ben will join. we'll propose a half-day workshop to walk through the export flow and artifact validation.
[08:53] Jordan: quick recap: i'll share SOC 2 Type II link and the high-level inventory; priya will provide controls mapping; marcus will set viewer access; leeza will coordinate the workshop with your ops team; ben will prepare Lyra system list. sound right?
[09:05] Alicia: yes. and please include estimated pricing for long-term log retention and the Trust Center export SLA.
[09:12] Jordan: noted. we'll follow up.
[09:18] Tom: thanks everyone.
[09:20] Jordan: thanks all — we'll send notes and action items.

(End of recording)
questions: Can Redwood provide SOC 2 Type II now?
How does customer-managed KMS work across regions?
Can auditor access be limited to view-only and time-boxed?
Is long-term log retention (7+ years) supported for pharma records?
notes: Priorities: controls mapping, Trust Center access, KMS BYOK, long retention pricing
